beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — BH3 priming and the cliff metaphor
beats.narration_text: Some cancer cells are sitting right at the edge of the apoptosis cliff — their pro-death levels are nearly at the threshold, held back only by BCL-2. They are called primed. A primed cell needs only one thing removed to go over the edge.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — two-meter diagram: left meter SKY fill near threshold with BLUE clamp; right meter VERM fill past threshold with death glyph; arrow connecting them; label: BCL-2 = the clamp

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — venetoclax, BH3 profiling, clinical use
beats.narration_text: Venetoclax removes BCL-2's restraint. In primed cells, that is enough — the fill rises past the threshold and the cell dies. In unprimed cells, the fill is far below the threshold; removing BCL-2 is not sufficient. BH3 profiling measures how close to the cliff each cell is. The drug does not push — it removes the last handhold.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — stat card: BH3 profiling → mitochondrial priming → predicts venetoclax response; primed = near threshold; unprimed = far below

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the venetoclax-priming plate from plates underscore gen dot py p20 into Manim. Two meters side by side — tall rounded column outlines in GRAY — connected by a center arrow. Left meter: a SKY filled rectangle rising from the bottom to just below a dashed threshold line near the top, with a BLUE clamp rectangle pressing down at the top, and an ORANGE triangle drug plug at left with an arrow pointing at the clamp. Right meter: a VERM fill rising past the threshold — no clamp — and a VERM death glyph polygon at top-right with an arrow from the fill. Animate left to right: left meter first, then arrow grows, then right meter.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_VenetoclaxPriming class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The two meters are identical column outlines — GRAY rectangles with rounded corners, no fill — placed at x minus two point five and x plus two point five. The fill inside each meter is a second rectangle, shorter than the column, aligned to the bottom, given the fill colour — SKY for the left primed meter, VERM for the right tipped meter. The dashed threshold line is a DashedLine drawn at a fixed y-position near the top of the column. The BLUE clamp is a filled BLUE rectangle sitting at the top of the left meter's column — it is just a rectangle, nothing complicated. The ORANGE plug is a Triangle pointing right, at the left edge of the left meter, with an Arrow from it to the clamp. The death glyph is a six-point irregular Polygon in VERM at the upper-right of the right meter with an Arrow from the fill top. The choreography is strictly sequential: left meter column, fill, threshold, clamp, plug — then center arrow grows — then right meter column, fill, threshold, then death glyph.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_VenetoclaxPriming
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; VERM="#D55E00"; ORANGE="#E69F00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_VenetoclaxPriming(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    col_h,col_w=4.5,1.4; thr_y=1.2
    # Left meter
    lc=RoundedRectangle(width=col_w,height=col_h,corner_radius=0.2,
      color=GRAY,fill_opacity=0,stroke_width=3).move_to([-2.5,0,0])
    lf=Rectangle(width=col_w-0.15,height=3.1,color=SKY,
      fill_color=SKY,fill_opacity=0.55,stroke_width=0.8
      ).align_to(lc,DOWN).shift(UP*0.07).set_x(-2.5)
    lt=DashedLine([-2.5-0.75,thr_y,0],[-2.5+0.75,thr_y,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.5,dash_length=0.12)
    clamp=Rectangle(width=col_w+0.2,height=0.42,color=BLUE,
      fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.6,stroke_width=3
      ).move_to([-2.5,lc.get_top()[1]-0.0,0])
    plug=Triangle(color=ORANGE,fill_color=ORANGE,fill_opacity=0.8,
      stroke_width=2).scale(0.35).rotate(-PI/2).move_to([-4.3,0.8,0])
    parr=Arrow([-3.9,0.8,0],[-2.85,clamp.get_center()[1],0],
      buff=0.05,color=ORANGE,stroke_width=2.5)
    # Center arrow
    carr=Arrow([-1.5,0,0],[0.5,0,0],buff=0,color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.8)
    # Right meter
    rc=RoundedRectangle(width=col_w,height=col_h,corner_radius=0.2,
      color=GRAY,fill_opacity=0,stroke_width=3).move_to([2.5,0,0])
    rf=Rectangle(width=col_w-0.15,height=4.1,color=VERM,
      fill_color=VERM,fill_opacity=0.55,stroke_width=0.8
      ).align_to(rc,DOWN).shift(UP*0.07).set_x(2.5)
    rt=DashedLine([2.5-0.75,thr_y,0],[2.5+0.75,thr_y,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.5,dash_length=0.12)
    dg=Polygon([3.6,1.5,0],[4.1,1.2,0],[3.9,0.9,0],[4.25,0.7,0],
      [4.0,0.65,0],[3.75,0.85,0],color=VERM,fill_color=VERM,fo=0.5,
      stroke_width=2.4)
    darr=Arrow([2.5,rf.get_top()[1],0],[3.5,1.4,0],
      buff=0.05,color=VERM,stroke_width=2.5)
    # Animate
    self.play(Create(lc),run_time=0.45)
    self.play(FadeIn(lf),Create(lt),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(FadeIn(clamp),FadeIn(plug),GrowArrow(parr),run_time=0.55)
    self.play(GrowArrow(carr),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(Create(rc),run_time=0.4)
    self.play(FadeIn(rf),Create(rt),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(FadeIn(dg),GrowArrow(darr),run_time=0.5); self.wait(0.8)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_VenetoclaxPriming — two meters, left primed below threshold, right tipped past
beats.narration_text: Run it. Left meter: the GRAY column outline in, SKY fill rising from the bottom to just below the dashed threshold, the BLUE clamp pressing down at the top, ORANGE plug approaching with an arrow. Then the center arrow grows. Right meter: GRAY column, VERM fill rising past the threshold — past the dashed line — then the death glyph in VERM with an arrow from the fill top. One plate, two states: primed and tipped.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: the drug plug should move along the arrow to the clamp — animate its position. The clamp FadeOuts when the plug arrives. Then the SKY fill should transform to VERM and rise past the threshold line — animate the height increasing. When the fill crosses the threshold, flash it. The death glyph should assemble from fragments — LaggedStart creating each polygon piece.

props.command:
claude "Revise: drug plug moves along arrow to clamp (animate position). Clamp
FadeOut. SKY fill transforms to VERM and rises past the threshold line
(animate height growing). Threshold line flashes as fill crosses it. Death glyph
assembles from fragments (LaggedStart)."

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with drug sweep and fill rise
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_VenetoclaxPrimingTip — plug moves, clamp out, fill rises, threshold flashes, glyph assembles
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The left meter is primed — fill below the threshold, clamp holds it. The drug plug moves along the arrow to the clamp and the clamp fades out. Then the fill rises — you watch it grow — and when it crosses the dashed threshold line, the line flashes. An arrow grows toward the death glyph. The death glyph assembles piece by piece. Proximity to the threshold is everything. The drug did not push the cell — it removed the last handhold.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: Proximity to the threshold is everything. The animation made priming physical: the fill was almost there, the clamp was the only thing holding it back. Venetoclax removes the clamp; the cell tips itself.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary card: BH3 priming = proximity to threshold; venetoclax = remove clamp; cell tips itself; 'the drug does not push'

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a third meter showing an unprimed cell — fill at only thirty percent of the column, far below the threshold — and animate what happens when the clamp is removed: the fill stays below threshold, no death glyph appears. Why run it? Because the contrast between primed and unprimed is the clinical prediction. When you animate all three states — primed below, primed and tipped, unprimed and surviving — you have a functional model of why BH3 profiling works as a biomarker. The fill level is not metaphor, it is the measurement: actual cytochrome-c release assay at sub-lethal BH3 peptide concentrations. The meter is the assay.

props.command:
claude "Add a third meter: unprimed cell — fill at 30%, far below threshold.
Remove the clamp (drug applied) — fill stays below, no death. Contrast
all three: primed-held, primed-tipped, unprimed-survived."
